headline: Highest risk is none-to-low overall: both open-source profiles are non-runnable, filesystem- and network-isolated, so no documented pairwise injection, leakage, or conflict pathway is present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible injection bridge is documented. Agent A has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, MCP, or browser surfaces, and Agent B exposes no I/O surfaces either. With both profiles lacking a shared channel, there is no pathway for A’s outputs to be ingested by B or vice versa.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF an orchestrator begins piping one agent’s raw output into the other’s prompt, the pathway becomes active.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared channels.
Do not add clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
If integration is needed, insert a sanitizer/formatter step.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any future shared messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, filesystem access, or network egress. Agent A cannot read or write files and Agent B exposes no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented route for sensitive data to move between them or out to a backend.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem access to shared sensitive data, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either profile later lists PHI, secrets, or regulated data classes, the severity may increase.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of both runtimes.
Avoid mounting shared folders.
Disable any future upload or sync features.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is present. Agent A cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses; Agent B has no documented write, git, or mutable-resource permissions. Without shared mutable state, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk becomes active.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable OAuth scopes or database writes, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not grant shared repo or directory writes.
Avoid concurrent mutation workflows.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented evidence that B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, and neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority. Because both agents are non-runnable and lack I/O surfaces, the cascade pathway is not established; uncertainty here does not justify escalation.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding A’s outputs directly into B without verification, reassess.
IF either agent gains authority to send emails, commit code, or execute tasks, cascade risk increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require explicit verification of any facts passed onward.
Keep both agents non-executing.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, unverified, and touch no data classes; there is no indication of PHI, EU PII, residency constraints, or retention differences. The other agent is not cited separately because no regulated-data pathway exists to compare.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data classes, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency, retention, or certification requirements are added later, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Review jurisdictional requirements if data classes change.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for future regulated workloads.
